children: Equity benchmarks managed to close moderately higher amid range-bound trading on September 4, with market breadth remaining positive. About 1,808 shares advanced, compared with 1,433 declining shares on the NSE. The market is likely to trade within the previous week’s range in the short term. Here are some short-term trading ideas to consider:
Rajesh Palviya, Senior Vice President Research (Head of Research) at Axis Securities

On the weekly chart, IFCI surpassed the "multiple resistance zone" of Rs 90-93 on a closing basis, along with huge volumes indicating resumption of the prior uptrend. The daily and weekly Bollinger Band buy signal indicates increased momentum.

The stock is well placed above its 20, 50, 100 and 200-day simple moving averages (SMAs). These averages are also inching up along with the price rise, which reconfirms the bullish trend. The daily, weekly and monthly Relative Strength Index (RSI) is in favourable territory, indicating rising strength across all time frames.

On the weekly chart, Balaji Amines confirmed a 'flag' formation breakout at Rs 2,455 levels on a closing basis, along with rising volumes indicating increased participation in the rally. The daily, weekly and monthly RSI is in favourable territory, indicating rising strength across all time frames.
The stock is well placed above its 20, 50, 100 and 200-day simple moving averages (SMAs). These averages are also inching up along with the price rise, which reconfirms the bullish trend.
Central Mine Planning & Design Institute | CMP: Rs 243.92

On the daily chart, Central Mine Planning & Design Institute confirmed a "down-sloping trendline" breakout at Rs 241 level on a closing basis. Huge volumes accompanied this breakout, indicating increased participation. The daily RSI is in positive mode indicating rising strength.
Hitesh Rathi, Technical Analyst (Equity & Derivatives) at Angel One

ACME Solar Holdings remains in a structural uptrend, and the consolidation breakout observed on Friday signals a resumption of its uptrend. The recent consolidation has also resulted in cooling down of its overbought technical indicators, offering a suitable entry opportunity on a relatively strong stock.
A bullish DTB (double top buy) pattern breakout on the 1%*3 Daily Point and figure chart, provides further confirmation of an uptrend resumption. Hence, the buying is recommended around Rs 419-415.

The recent short-term blip, followed by a 2-month price consolidation offers a lucrative opportunity to enter into a relatively outperforming stock. At the same time, a price volume breakout provides further credence to a resumption in its prior uptrend. A Point and figure support pattern formation near the Rs 1,850 mark, signal the presence of strong demand at lower levels in Wockhardt.

A multi-brick breakout on the 3% Renko chart provides further confirmation of a breakout across difference charting systems. Hence, the buying is recommended around Rs 2,088-2,080, with a stop-loss of Rs 1,769, and target of Rs 2,300-2,350.

Indraprastha Gas is pointing towards early signs of a trend reversal following a sustained downtrend in the stock. The formation of a Bullish Pattern Retest on the 1% × 3% Daily Point & Figure chart, followed by a Bullish Bear Trap, indicates the presence of strong demand at lower levels. A breakout from the consolidation range on the Daily candlestick chart points towards a shift in control from sellers towards buyers in the intermediate term.

Further confirmation comes from a trendline breakout on the 14-day RSI, indicating that the stock is now benefiting from improving bullish momentum. Hence, the buying is recommended around Rs 158-157, with a stop-loss of Rs 144, and target of Rs 175-180.
Jatin Gedia, VP - Technical Research at Teji Mandi Investment Technologies

Reliance Industries has formed a double bottom at the Rs 1,250 level. It formed a Leading diagonal from the July low (Rs 1,249.80) suggesting the start of a fresh leg of upmove. After that, it corrected towards the 61.8% retracement level (Rs 1,272) making a higher bottom and thereby completing wave 2 or wave B.

Last week the stock started the next leg of the upmove (wave 3 or wave C), which could take it towards the Rs 1,377 -1,406 zone, representing the 127.2% and 161.8% Fibonacci extension targets. On the weekly chart, the stock formed an Engulfing Bull candlestick pattern, suggesting a shift in control from sellers to buyers.

The weekly momentum indicator had a positive crossover and now the daily momentum indicator is also in sync, suggesting that a strong upward trend is likely in the stock. Volume was the highest compared to the last ten weeks. Thus, the price pattern, volume, and momentum setup suggest that the stock is poised for an upmove during the week.

Tata Communications was in the process of retracing the five wave upmove from Rs 1,322 to Rs 2,110. It retraced towards the 61.8% level (Rs 1,645) of the rally marking the end of the pullback and has resumed its primary uptrend. It has started to form higher highs and higher Lows on the daily charts suggesting a trend reversal from down to up.

MACD has triggered a fresh positive crossover from below the equilibrium line, suggesting the start of a new upward cycle. We expect the stock to rally towards Rs 1,863 which is the 161.8% Fibonacci extension target.
Sun Pharmaceutical Industries September Futures | CMP: 1,903.5

Sun Pharmaceutical has been forming lower highs and lower lows on the daily charts, suggesting a downtrend. Pullback towards Rs 1,962 - the 50% Fibonacci retracement level—was sold into, suggesting the resumption of the next leg of the down move.

In terms of price pattern the stock broke down from a bearish flag pattern on the daily charts which is a trend continuation pattern. MACD has triggered a fresh negative crossover which is a sell signal. Thus, considering the price pattern breakdown and the bearish momentum setup, the stock is poised for a decline.
